title: Extracting Decision Model and Notation models from text using deep learning techniques

source_record_provenance.record_title: Extracting Decision Model and Notation models from text using deep learning techniques

satisfied_inclusion_points: Abstract explicitly states the study uses NLP deep learning techniques to extract decision models from text.
Abstract describes an automatic sentence classifier and a decision dependency extractor (BERT and Bi-LSTM-CRF) applied to text.
uncertain_points: The title/abstract does not clearly state that the extracted artifacts are process models (it focuses on Decision Model and Notation, i.e., decision models).
Unclear from title/abstract whether the work targets process extraction as defined by the review (business/process models) versus decision-model extraction specifically.
evidence_highlights: "This paper studies how NLP deep learning techniques can extract decision models from text faster."
"we study and evaluate an automatic sentence classifier and a decision dependency extractor using NLP deep learning models (BERT and Bi-LSTM-CRF)."
"We conclude that BERT can be used for the (semi)-automatic extraction of decision models from text."
stage1_review.decision_rationale: The title and abstract clearly describe using NLP deep learning methods to extract Decision Model and Notation models from natural-language text, so the core task of extracting structured models from text is supported. However, the review's scope concerns process extraction (process/process-model representations). The abstract focuses on decision models (DMN) rather than explicit process models, leaving uncertainty whether this paper fits the process-extraction topic exactly. Per Stage 1 rules, defer final inclusion decision to Stage 2.

These facts directly satisfy the Stage 2 inclusion criteria (paper type, originality, NLP for process/decision-model extraction, concrete method and experiments); no exclusion criteria are triggered.
